🧹 Nitpick comments (2)
libs/ui-lib/lib/cim/components/helpers/versions.ts (1)
`35-54`: **Unknown `labels.architecture` values short-circuit the fallback chain.** Because `??` is only bypassed by `null`/`undefined`, any non-nullish `labels.architecture` (including typos like `'muti'` or unrelated strings) will be selected, and then the switch `default` returns `undefined` without consulting `releaseTag`, `releaseImage`, or `metadata.name`. If the intent is "label is authoritative when present, otherwise parse other sources," this is fine; if the intent is "only trust known architecture values from the label," fallback parsing should run when the label value isn't recognized.
Possible refactor (only if label recognition should gate trust) ```diff - const cpuArch = - clusterImageSet?.metadata?.labels?.architecture ?? - getCPUArchFromReleaseString(clusterImageSet?.metadata?.labels?.['releaseTag']) ?? - getCPUArchFromReleaseString(clusterImageSet?.spec?.releaseImage) ?? - getCPUArchFromReleaseString(clusterImageSet?.metadata?.name) ?? - ''; + const candidates = [ + clusterImageSet?.metadata?.labels?.architecture, + getCPUArchFromReleaseString(clusterImageSet?.metadata?.labels?.['releaseTag']), + getCPUArchFromReleaseString(clusterImageSet?.spec?.releaseImage), + getCPUArchFromReleaseString(clusterImageSet?.metadata?.name), + ]; + const cpuArch = candidates.find((c) => !!c && normalize(c) !== undefined) ?? ''; ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. In `@libs/ui-lib/lib/cim/components/helpers/versions.ts` around lines 35 - 54, The current getCPUArchFromClusterImageSet uses labels.architecture with the nullish-coalescing operator (??), which accepts any non-null label including unknown/typo values and prevents falling back to getCPUArchFromReleaseString; update getCPUArchFromClusterImageSet so it first reads metadata.labels.architecture into a variable, validate it against the known CpuArchitecture values (and the 'x86-64' alias) and only accept it when recognized, otherwise continue to call getCPUArchFromReleaseString on releaseTag/releaseImage/metadata.name; ensure the switch or validation logic still returns CpuArchitecture.x86 for 'x86-64' and returns undefined only after all fallback parsing has been attempted. ```
libs/ui-lib/lib/cim/components/helpers/versions.test.ts (1)
`172-189`: **Nit: misleading variable name and suspected typos in this test.** - The variable `arm` is not actually an arm64 image — its releaseImage is `4.16.1-multi` and `labels.architecture` is `'muti'`. Consider renaming to `nonMatching` (or similar) for clarity. - `labels.architecture: 'muti'` and `releaseTag: '4.16.1-mutli'` look like unintended typos of `multi`. If the intent is to test that a `multi` image is filtered out for Nutanix, prefer the correctly spelled value so the test reflects a realistic input.
Suggested cleanup ```diff - const arm = makeClusterImageSet({ + const multi = makeClusterImageSet({ metadata: { name: 'nut-multi', - labels: { visible: 'true', releaseTag: '4.16.1-mutli', architecture: 'muti' }, + labels: { visible: 'true', releaseTag: '4.16.1-multi', architecture: 'multi' }, }, spec: { releaseImage: 'quay.io/ocp/release:4.16.1-multi' }, }); - const result = getOCPVersions([x86, arm], true); + const result = getOCPVersions([x86, multi], true); ```

In `@libs/ui-lib/lib/cim/components/helpers/versions.test.ts` around lines 172 - 189, The test "when isNutanix, keeps only x86_64 or x86-64 release images or matching architecture label" uses a misleading variable name `arm` and contains typos in its labels; update the second fixture created with makeClusterImageSet to a clearer name (e.g., `nonMatching`) and correct the typos so its labels and tag use "multi" consistently (labels.architecture: 'multi' and labels.releaseTag: '4.16.1-multi', plus spec.releaseImage: 'quay.io/ocp/release:4.16.1-multi') so the test input accurately represents a non-matching multi-arch image passed to getOCPVersions. ```
